title: 4GE1-style exam questions: Upland river landforms: V-shaped valleys, interlocking spurs and waterfalls (1.2c)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y10 lesson 28 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 28: Upland river landforms: V-shaped valleys, interlocking spurs and waterfalls (1.2c). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: 'Explain the formation of a waterfall and gorge.' Use a labelled sequence of three sketches and write in the portal response box.
questions.a: Hard over soft rock; undercutting by hydraulic action and abrasion; overhang collapses; plunge pool deepens; retreat forms gorge
questions.model: Teacher draws sketch 1: two rock layers with the river flowing over; labels 'hard dolerite' and 'softer limestone and shale'.

questions.q: Describe the features of a V-shaped valley and interlocking spurs using an OS map extract.
questions.a: Contours close together (steep sides) (1); V shape where contours point upstream (1); river winding between alternating spurs (1)

questions.q: Suggest why waterfalls are often in the upper course.
questions.a: Steep gradients and changes in rock type are common in uplands (1); vertical erosion is strongest there (1)

questions.q: Explain why upland valleys are V-shaped.
questions.a: The river erodes vertically (1); weathering and mass movement wear the sides (1); material slides into the river and is carried away, forming a V (1)
questions.model: Downwards: vertical erosion deepens the channel. Sideways: weathering loosens the valley sides. Down the slope: mass movement, then the river removes it. Result: a V.

questions.q: Name the hard rock at High Force.

questions.a: The deep pool eroded at the base of a waterfall

questions.q: Big question: how does a waterfall move upstream?
questions.a: Undercutting of soft rock makes the hard overhang collapse repeatedly, so the waterfall retreats, leaving a gorge
